item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00350","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C03","C02","C23"],"selected_candidate_label":"C03","confidence":0.94,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C03 plausibly supplied a material template for the child. Both are presidential appeals to the Vice President immediately before Senate action on numbered reorganization plans; both characterize the plans as administrative improvements, distinguish administrative organization from disputed substantive policy, answer opponents' objections and political framing, and conclude by urging favorable Senate action. C02 shares the specific National Labor Relations Board setting but lacks this drafting sequence. C23 contains a similar distinction between administrative organization and substantive policy, but in a different legislative context.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"UNDERSTAND that the Senate will shortly vote on reorganization plan number twelve... I urge that the Senate give the plan its approval.","parent_excerpt":"I am informed that the Senate will soon take action on Reorganization Plans No. 1 and No. 2 of 1949... I trust, therefore, that the Senate will permit Reorganization Plans No. 1 and No. 2 to become effective.","explanation":"Both letters open with impending Senate consideration of numbered reorganization plans and close with a direct request for favorable Senate action."},{"child_excerpt":"Plan twelve will correct an administratively unworkable organizational set-up... Plan twelve is in the best interests of sound government organization and administration.","parent_excerpt":"These plans are of great importance in improving the organization and administration of the Federal Government... greater efficiency and economy","explanation":"The child reuses the parent's core administrative-reform justification, adapting it to the Labor Board."},{"child_excerpt":"The issues now involved... do not... go to the substance of the controversy over the Taft-Hartley Act, as opponents... have attempted to argue.","parent_excerpt":"These plans propose administrative changes, not changes in legislative policy... Those groups who are opposing these plans on such grounds are creating imaginary difficulties.","explanation":"This is a close conceptual and rhetorical parallel: both rebut opposition by separating an administrative reorganization from the contested substantive policy surrounding it."}]}
